## Drift

PR #27344 (#27237) makes an unresolved or refused `credentialRef` degrade its instance instead of failing boot, and adds a credential door whose `DELETE` tears a live instance down. These texts still state the old rule or omit the new one:

1. **`docs/adr/0097-declarative-connector-instances.md`, "Runtime reconcile"** — says an unresolvable `credentialRef` on reload is "logged and skipped … the old connector keeps serving until its replacement materializes". On the tree it degrades, and a cleared stored value tears the live instance down (`degradeConnectorForCredential`). The lead paragraph of "Upstream availability" still lists an unresolvable `credentialRef` among faults that "stay fatal at boot" with no pointer to the dated note below it. Ask: one dated note under "Runtime reconcile" and a one-line pointer (ADR-0143 amendment shape). Tier H.
2. **`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`, `clearConnectorCredential`** — its refusal list omits the `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` the clear path answers when the store cannot be read or written (`ConnectorCredentialUnavailableError`).
3. **`content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx:361`** — comment "a reference, resolved at boot".
4. **`packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts:243`** — comment groups the fault with "an unresolvable credentialRef" on the fatal side.
5. **`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/integration-system.json:1943, 1992`** (item `integration-system.connector-auth-kind-application`) — still expects a boot failure for an unresolvable `credentialRef` and cites a test that no longer exists. QA lane.

## Filing facts

- reach: authors and AI authoring passes reading the ADR, contract docs and docs page; the QA checklist grades the old behaviour.
- Dedupe: #27237 / PR #27344. No open card on these texts.
